title: A small, stainless-steel sieve optimized for laboratory beaker-based extraction of microplastics from environmental samples
author: Nakajima, Lindsay, et al.

steps.title: Prepare stainless‑steel sieve
steps.instruction: Obtain the small stainless‑steel sieve (55 mm external diameter, 88 mm height) with a 32 µm mesh screen positioned 10 mm above the cylinder base; optionally place a magnetic stir bar in the space below the mesh.

steps.title: Generate size‑fractionated microplastics
steps.instruction: Mill polystyrene plates using a plastic‑grinder (PCL‑2 M, Osaka Chemical) and size‑fractionate the resulting particles with stainless‑steel screens of 100 µm, 500 µm and 1000 µm mesh openings to obtain two size classes (100–500 µm and 500–1000 µm).

steps.title: Set up experimental replicates
steps.instruction: For each size class, place exactly 30 microplastic particles onto either the prepared sieve or a PTFE filter (Whatmann, 1.2 µm) housed in a glass filter holder; prepare 10 replicates per size class.

steps.title: Remove inorganic carbonates with HCl
steps.instruction: Immerse the sieve in a beaker containing 1 N HCl, and for filter samples rinse the filter into a beaker of 1 N HCl; allow the reaction to proceed for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Rinse after acid treatment
steps.instruction: Retrieve the sieve and rinse it with MilliQ water using a squirt bottle; for filter samples, filter the HCl‑treated material onto a new PTFE filter and rinse the filter with distilled water.

steps.title: Digest organic matter
steps.instruction: Transfer all solids (sieve contents and filter residues) into a beaker containing a solution of 0.5 M Fe(II) plus 30 % hydrogen peroxide; heat the solution on a hot plate at 75 °C for 30 minutes.

steps.title: Collect microplastics after digestion
steps.instruction: After the 30‑minute heating, filter the entire contents of the sieve and the digestion beaker onto a fresh PTFE filter to recover the microplastics.

steps.title: Count recovered microplastics
steps.instruction: Examine the filtered microplastics under a microscope and count only the experimentally added particles (distinguished by color and shape).

steps.title: Statistical analysis of results
steps.instruction: Compare collection rates and processing times between sieve and filter methods using Student’s t‑test; consider differences significant at P < 0.05.
